meta.description: Measures how loud a room is, from a small microphone board: the sound level, a spectrum by pitch and a calibrated level in dB SPL.

m5stack-atom-echos3r.description: A palm-sized ESP32-S3 board with a microphone, a sound chip and Wi-Fi, powered over USB.
m5stack-atom-echos3r.does: Runs ESPHome as a room sound sensor. Every second it reports the loudness and the loudest peak, five times a second a spectrum in 31 bands from deep bass to treble, and it can stream a faster reading on demand. It listens only: the speaker amplifier on the board stays off.

m5stack-led-strip-sk6812.description: An addressable 5 V RGB LED strip, 60 LEDs per metre, that plugs into the board's Grove port.
m5stack-led-strip-sk6812.does: Lights up with the music the sound sensor hears: the board itself draws it, so there is no delay through a server. Six styles, a palette and an intensity are set from the board's own settings in Home Assistant.

level.title: Sound level

strip.title: Music strip
strip.look_help:
- **Brightness** (the slider under the strip): the dimmer. It sets how much light the strip gives, not its colours.
- **Style**: what the strip draws. Pulse and Glow light the whole strip; Bands, Spectrum and Heat spread the frequencies along it; Centre meter is a level bar; Ripple sends a wave on each beat.
- **Palette**: the colours the styles use. *pastel* is soft and blends with the room; *custom* uses the colours in Custom palette.
- **Custom palette**: 2 to 5 colours as #rrggbb, separated by commas; the first is for quiet sound or bass, the last for loud sound or treble.
- **Pastel**: mixes every colour toward white. Raise it when the colours look too vivid.
- **Intensity**: how much the music moves the brightness. At 0 % the strip glows steadily and only its colours follow the music; at 100 % quiet parts go dark and loud parts light up fully. In Heat, at 100 % the quietest frequencies fade out; with the *single* palette that is one colour, dark where the music is quiet.
strip.layout_help:
- **Bass position**: where the low notes go. *centre* and *ends* mirror the picture around the middle of the strip; *start* puts the bass at the strip's beginning (the end with the cable) and the treble at the far end; *end* the other way round.
- **Mounting**: *front* for a strip you look at (sharp); *wall* or *floor* for one that lights a surface (smoother, blurred into a wash).
- **LEDs in use** and **First LED**: which part of the strip lights up; the rest stays dark.
strip.sound_help:
- **Sensitivity**: how loud the music has to be. Lower it (down to −40 dB) when the strip is too busy or stays at its loudest colour; raise it for quiet listening.
- **Range**: how big a difference in loudness the colours and the brightness span. Small (10–20 dB) shows small differences between the frequencies; large (40–60 dB) is calmer.
- **Auto gain**: follows the volume over about 10 seconds, so the strip moves at any volume. Leave it on.
- **Attack** and **Release**: how fast the strip reacts when the sound rises, and how slowly it fades.
- **Beat strength**: how strong the flash or the ripple on a beat is.
- **Beat sensitivity**: how readily a bass hit counts as a beat. Raise it when beats are missed, lower it when the strip flashes without one.
strip.power_help:
- **Power limit**: the most current the strip may draw. 500 mA when it takes its power from the board's cable; the supply's rating when it has its own 5 V supply. The strip dims itself to stay under it.
- **Current**: what the strip draws now, an estimate every 10 seconds.
- **Reset settings**: puts every setting of the strip on this page back to its default.
strip.automation_help:
- **Follow music**: turns the strip on when music plays and off after the off delay.
- **Off delay**: how long the strip stays on after the music stops (0 means 30 seconds).
- **Follow effect**: the style the strip starts with; *keep* starts the last one.
- **Ambient**: sets the brightness from the room's light, dim in a dark room and brighter in daylight. Dark and bright lux are the light levels, min and max the brightness at them.
